title: Rodoslovno stablo obitelji Franceschi
source: Family chart held by David Defranceski, «Rodoslovno stablo obitelji Franceschi» — the Omiš line. Twenty generations, 1318 to 1992.
caveat: A made family tree, not a register. The medieval generations carry offices and dates that no document has been checked for here, and should be read as the family's own account of itself until they are. The 17th- to 19th-century names, by contrast, match independent records found for this archive.

posjednik; wife a contessa M. Cambj

siblings: Girolamo b. 1789 and don Giovanni 1810–1882, beside Antonio 1801–1877
Frane 1826–1896 (wife M. Caralipeo), Nikola 1835–1914 (wife Theresa), Josip 1844–1904 posjednik (wife a countess A. Grubišić), beside Ivan 1829–1895
Josip 1879–1941, Emil 1886–1960 (mr. ph.), Dinko 1887–1893, Stjepan 1887–1927 (wife Stefania Lelas), Ante 1893–1936 (wife Dijaković)
matches: Carlo De Franceschi's history and the Imotski monograph both record a Gaspar de Franceschi at Omiš in 1590, owner of the warship Vascello and later admiral of the fleet. The chart gives him dates and a wife.
The same dates, to the year, as the Zuane Ivan Franceschi who sheltered six hundred Imotski refugees from January 1715, raised 250 men, took the town in July 1717 and was granted the Perinuša estate.

This matters. The Imotski monograph derives the name Perinuša from a Perinović family of Zadar brought in as stewards. But the by-name «Perini» is in this family's own direct line a century before Imotski — which is a simpler reason why Kačić Miošić sang of the hero of 1717 as «Perinović Ive».

Independently reconstructed for this archive from the FamilySearch index: a Francesco Franceschi and Maria Caralipeo at Almissa with eleven recorded children between 1854 and 1877 — the largest household in the whole reconstruction.
Also in the index: an Antonio Franceschi and Antonia Radmillovich at Almissa.

Four generations hold Zadar offices — notary, municipal archivist, port salt office. The received family account lists «Zadar → Rijeka and Bakar» as one of its four directions; this chart says Zadar is where the Dalmatian line came from.
omittedNote: The chart runs to a boy born in 1992. Everyone on it without a recorded death is omitted from this build — 3 generations at the top, and the same rule applied to the collateral names. They are on the original, which is a private family document; this is a public one.

gazzetta1840.heading: A vineyard at Almissa, 1840 — and the first Omiš Defranceschi this archive has found in print
gazzetta1840.lead: The Austrian National Library's newspaper search reported nine issues carrying both «Defranceschi» and «Buccari». Its page viewer is behind a bot check this archive will not answer, so David fetched the oldest of the nine himself: the **Gazzetta di Zara of 4 August 1840**, eight pages, the official gazette of Dalmatia. One occurrence of the name, and it is in exactly the right district.

rows.text:
An **avviso** of the Imperial-Royal **Pretura d'Almissa** — the magistracy of **Omiš** — dated **6 July 1840** and signed **Gio: Maria Ipsich, Pretore**, announcing the sale of state property by public auction in the Pretura's office on **16, 17 and 18 September 1840 at ten in the morning**. Four lots, all vineyard or arable, all at a place called **Strane in Vrisovec**, and each listed with the tenant who held it. The second lot:

«**Un terreno vignato, chiamato Strane in Vrisovec, dell'estesa di vreteni 2 circa, tenuto a colonia al quarto da D. Nicolò Defranceschi. La voce fiscale è di fi. 8 k. 20.**» — a vineyard called Strane at Vrisovec, of about two *vreteni*, **held in colonia at the quarter by D. Nicolò Defranceschi.** Fiscal value 8 florins 20 kreuzer.

rows.lab: What «tenuto a colonia al quarto» means
rows.text: The **colonato**, the Dalmatian sharecropping tenure: the *colono* works the land and renders a share of the crop, here **a quarter**, to the owner. So Nicolò Defranceschi was not the owner — he was the working tenant of a state-owned vineyard, and the state was selling it out from under him. His neighbours in the same list are the heirs of Matteo Benković, Gian Francesco Pavišić and a Radmillović, and none of them carries an honorific. **Only Defranceschi is given a «D.»** — Don, or Dominus — which in a Dalmatian public notice marks a priest or a gentleman among peasants.

Almissa is Omiš. This page has the Dalmatian family at Omiš from Francesco the Venetian's foundation plaque of 1584, and follows it to Imotski and Perinuša after 1717 — but almost everything it holds for the nineteenth century comes from a family tree rather than a document. **Here is a Defranceschi at Omiš in 1840, named, with a plot of land, a tenure, a valuation and a date, in the official gazette of the province.** He is the first of them this archive has found in print rather than in a pedigree.

rows.lab: And a correction to the Bakar lead
rows.text: This issue also carries **Buccari** — but in a wholly unconnected notice, from the magistrate of «la libera città marittima e commerciale e distretto porto franco di Buccari», dated 7 February 1840, at the instance of one Maria Carina. **The two words are pages apart and have nothing to do with each other.** Which means the search that produced «nine issues on Defranceschi and Buccari» was matching the two words **anywhere in the same issue**, not together — and a gazette prints notices from every district in the province. **The Bakar lead is therefore much weaker than it looked**, and the other eight issues should be read expecting coincidence rather than a household.

gazzetta1840.source_gdz: «Gazzetta di Zara», anno IX, 4 August 1840, eight pages — the official gazette of the Kingdom of Dalmatia, printed at Zadar.
